dek: A radio host and Doc's Sports handicapper who says he has 35 years in the business. Packages run from $25 for a day of props to $850 for an NBA season. The guarantee pays in credit or extra time, the record on the sales page is a set of chosen runs, and his one public contest record this fall was close to even.

short_answer: Tony George is a real, long running handicapper and radio host. VSiN named him in the invited field of its 2026 Circa Friday Football Invitational, and he sells picks through Doc's Sports, a store that names its company and gives a phone number and email. In that narrow sense the service is legitimate.

Whether his paid picks make money is a separate question. The Doc's Sports page lists rankings and runs such as "CBB 6-1 / +$2040 run" and "Up 25 Units YTD," all chosen by the seller, and we found no full, time stamped log of every pick he has sold.

The only third party number we found is his entry in the Circa Invitational contest, reposted on a forum on 7 Nov 2026 at 28-25-3, 17th of 25. That is a small sample of football sides, not his paid card, but it sits much closer to break even than the sales page story. We found no independent buyer reviews at all.
pricing_intro: All rows below were on Tony George's Doc's Sports page on 16 Nov 2026. A separate CappersPicks listing under the name Sports Audio Shows shows daily $20, weekly $65, monthly $250 and yearly $650 with no date, so we do not treat those as current prices.
pricing: One weekend, ends the following Wednesday; "backed by our profit guarantee"
Self extend if the package does not produce a profit

NBA One Week / One Month / Full Season (Early Bird)
NHL One Week / One Month / Complete Season (Early Bird)
"We guarantee you a daily profit"; $30 credit next morning if not
guarantee: The page sells a "profit guarantee," but the remedy is never cash. On the college basketball day package, a $30 account credit is applied the next morning if the day does not make at least $40, so a small winning day still counts as a failure. The daily props package promises a daily profit and gives a $30 credit if it misses. On football, NBA and NHL packages of a week or longer, a losing package can be extended for free through the store's self extend program.

We found no separate guarantee or refund policy page linked from his profile, and no cash refund terms. A buyer who loses money betting the picks gets more picks or store credit. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered, and they are usually far larger than the package price.

claims_note: His experience claim holds together over time: 25 years in a 2017 post, 27 in a 2019 Gambling911 article, 35 on today's page. The radio career is also described in a 2017 Gambling911 article about his SB Nation Radio show.

The rankings are another matter. They come from monitors and from Doc's Sports itself, the store that sells his picks, and none of the pages we opened links to the underlying records. A 2019 Gambling911 article repeats a BetFirms claim that his NFL picks hit 65% since late September 2015; the article calls him a friend of the site and links to his paid picks, so it is not an independent audit.
Every run on the sales page starts and stops where the seller chose. Every handicapper has a hot stretch somewhere.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: one contest. VSiN lists Tony George in the 2026 Circa Friday Football Invitational field, and a standings table reposted on TheRX on 7 Nov 2026 showed him at 28-25-3, 17th of 25 entries. That is about 53% against the spread on a small sample, and the repost does not say which week it was last updated. We did not check it against the contest's own page.

What the seller publishes: the Doc's Sports page shows yearly rankings, chosen runs and member notes such as "Lost out on Saturday" in the NFL. These are graded by the store that sells the picks, so they are marketing, not an audit.
We found no full, time stamped log of every Tony George pick with the line, the odds and the release time, and no court or regulator record about him.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Tony George pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Tony George performs.
our_data.context: For scale: his contest entry was 28-25-3 in the reposted table. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: We found no independent buyer reviews of Tony George. Below is what does exist and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found no posts from people who say they bought Tony George picks and report how it went, good or bad. Our searches of Reddit's r/sportsbook and r/sportsbetting and of the big betting forums turned up only reposts of his plays, a TheRX thread about Doc's Sports that never names him, and a public contest table showing him close to even this fall. Our own collection of forum and X posts from 2026 holds many mentions of his name, all of them copied picks with no buyer comment. No complaints and no praise: buyer evidence is simply missing, so this page rests on the seller's own claims and one contest.
A TheRX member reposted the Circa Invitational standings, which showed Tony George at 28-25-3 and 17th of 25 entries. No one in the post commented on him.

A Gambling911 article praised his record, quoting a BetFirms claim of a 65% NFL hit rate since late September 2015 and reporting one 6-1 baseball night. The article calls him a friend of the site and carries links to buy his picks, so it is promotion, not a customer report.

His Doc's Sports page shows no customer testimonials. A TheRX thread about Doc's Sports running from Dec 2025 to Aug 2026 does not mention him, and the Reddit archive post search found no thread about his service. A Sportsbook Review thread that search results say tracked his 2021 picks did not open for us, so we leave it out.

conflicts: The records on the sales page are graded and published by Doc's Sports, the store that takes the money.
Gambling911, one of the few outside sites that writes about him, describes him as a friend of the site and links to his paid picks.
The CappersPicks listing for Sports Audio Shows says CappersPicks is located in Antigua, West Indies, and its prices differ from Doc's Sports. Check which store you are buying from.
strengths: A real, documented career in sports radio and handicapping, and a place in VSiN's invited Circa contest field.
Every Doc's Sports package shows a clear price, length and remedy.
One public contest record exists that anyone can follow.
concerns: No full public record of his paid picks. Every number on the sales page is chosen and graded by the seller.
The guarantee pays in credit or extra time, never cash, and the college basketball day package counts a small win as a loss.
His one third party record this season sat near break even, 28-25-3.
No independent buyer reviews to weigh, good or bad.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real handicapper and radio host, sold through Doc's Sports with published prices, and VSiN named him in its 2026 Circa contest field. We could not verify that his paid picks win over time, we found no buyer reviews either way, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
How much does Tony George cost?

On 16 Nov 2026 Doc's Sports listed $25 for a day of props, $30 for a day of college basketball, $99 for a football weekend or a week of college or NBA basketball, and season packages from $495 to $850.
Does Tony George have a verified record?
No. The sales page shows rankings and chosen runs graded by Doc's Sports. The only third party number we found is his Circa Invitational entry, 28-25-3 in a table reposted on 7 Nov 2026.

You get a known name with a long radio career and a credit or extension if a package loses. What is unproven is whether his picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays, and nothing refunds the package or your betting losses.
